svg.title: One user is a loop, not a firehose
svg.desc: A single virtual user's twenty-second loop drawn on a timeline. Three requests are sent: load the feed at zero seconds, open a post at about five seconds, and a like at about eleven seconds which only happens on fifteen percent of loops. Between them are long reading pauses of three to seven and three to eight seconds, which occupy almost the whole loop. The requests are thin ticks and the reading is wide shaded bands, so the drawing shows that think time dominates. Underneath, the arithmetic: about two to three requests in roughly twenty seconds gives about 0.1 requests per second per user, and one thousand such users were measured at 83 requests per second, against a model estimate near 100. Motion timing is illustrative, not a production measurement.
svg.text: ONE USER IS A LOOP, NOT A FIREHOSE
The pauses are the model. Change them and the headline number changes while the server is untouched.
2 to 3 requests, in roughly 20 seconds of loop
Almost all of that time is a person reading, not a server working
So one concurrent user offers about 0.1 requests per second
Model says about 100 req/s at 1,000 users. Measured: 83. The gap is the spread in the pauses.
